policy: Recommended extensions: outside repositories the Studio owner reviewed and judged useful as an engine or knowledge source next to Studio. Each one is pinned to a reviewed version, installed only on the user's explicit request with its own installer, and never becomes part of Studio: Studio's routes, rules and quality checks stay in charge.

statuses.native: Installs and runs in this host with the commands given
statuses.desktop_only: Only in the desktop app of this host, not in its web or mobile app
statuses.not_supported: Cannot run in this host; the reason says why and where it can
statuses.manual: No installer runs in this host; the user adds the named files by hand (for example as a project's knowledge)

extensions.name: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
extensions.gives: Reverse engineering of software the user may analyse: native binaries (with Hopper, Ghidra or IDA), JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Android packages, websites through the browser's DevTools, network captures; every finding comes with its evidence and unknowns
extensions.studio_uses: Optional depth when the user wants to know how a feature or an effect of an app or a website is built and Studio's own web motion probe is not enough: an Electron or desktop app, a bundled script, a source map. For a web animation, the web motion probe answers first
extensions.not_for: Image or prompt reverse engineering (that is Image Prompt Architect's reference reconstruction), copying another product's code or assets, bypassing protection, licences or logins

requires.note: Node.js 22.19+, 24.11+ or 26+, with npm
A Chrome-family browser for website analysis
Hopper, Ghidra or IDA only for native binaries; JavaScript and .NET analysis need none

extensions.rights: Analyse only software and sites the user owns or may examine, within the law and the target's licence and terms; the results grant no right to the original code, data or design. Studio uses findings to learn a technique and builds its own version; it never copies code, assets or text.

codex.after: Restart Codex; the REA tools must appear in the new session

claude_code.after: Restart Claude Code; the REA tools must appear in the new session

claude_apps.writes: the Claude desktop app's claude_desktop_config.json (with a backup) and ~/.agents/skills/reverse-engineer-anything
claude_apps.after: Run the commands in a terminal on the same computer, then restart the desktop app; the web and mobile apps cannot run a local MCP server

chatgpt.reason: REA is a local MCP server that runs on the user's computer; ChatGPT chats cannot start one. Use it from Codex or Claude Code on the same computer

chatgpt_work.reason: REA is a local (stdio) MCP server; ChatGPT Work connects remote connectors, and its code sandbox is not a host REA supports. Use it from Codex or Claude Code

extensions.gives: Logo discovery, concept comparison, SVG craft and optical refinement; reference search, SVG audit, concept/test sheets and icon exports. Upstream plugin version 1.4.4.
extensions.studio_uses: Studio bundles the reusable Logo Design tools, references, templates and catalogue within Static Graphic Design Creator. This optional entry installs the original separate workflow. Reference trademark SVGs retain their separate rights.
extensions.not_for: Automatic trademark clearance, guaranteed originality, production approval from a score, replacing the requested image/vector route, or copying reference marks.

requires.note: Read the full pinned checkout and retain LICENSE plus TRADEMARKS.md.
Node.js 22.20.0+ with npm, as required by the pinned skills CLI 1.7.2, for the Codex installation route.
Python 3.9+ for scripts. PNG output needs an available renderer (for example Chromium, CairoSVG or Inkscape); none is installed by Studio.

extensions.rights: MIT covers code and documentation, not the 1,432 reference trademark SVGs. Study construction without copying marks; a resemblance search is not clearance. Retain root LICENSE and TRADEMARKS.md, which upstream skill-only packaging omits.

extensions.name: Agent Reach
extensions.gives: A command-line layer that installs, checks and routes to tools for reading the web: web pages through Jina Reader, YouTube metadata and transcripts, RSS, public GitHub and Exa search through an MCP setup (mcporter); its doctor names the working route per channel
extensions.studio_uses: Optional research reach for Research Evidence in a shell host, when the host's own web tools cannot read a page, a YouTube transcript or a feed the brief depends on (a client's or competitor's site, a video's wording, a public changelog). Only the channels that need no login
extensions.not_for: Any channel that needs cookies, tokens or a logged-in browser session (X/Twitter, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, Xiaohongshu, Boss Zhipin): Studio never exports cookies, never uses spare accounts and never automates a platform against its terms. Not for bulk scraping, personal data or content the user may not use

requires.note: Python 3.10+ with pipx (or a virtual environment)
Node.js with npm only for mcporter, which the Exa search channel uses

extensions.rights: Read only public pages and feeds the user may access, within each site's terms and robots rules; Jina Reader and Exa are separate services with their own terms, and Exa may need its own key or plan (Unknown at review). What is read is evidence for Studio's research, cited with its source and date, never copied into deliverables as the user's own content.

codex.writes: the pipx environment, ~/.agent-reach/ (config, mode 600), the skill in ~/.agents/skills and, for Exa, a mcporter MCP configuration
codex.after: Start a new Codex session; set up only the channels that need no login

claude_code.writes: the pipx environment, ~/.agent-reach/ (config, mode 600), the skill in ~/.claude/skills and, for Exa, a mcporter MCP configuration
claude_code.after: Start a new conversation; set up only the channels that need no login

extensions.name: Huashu Art Motion (alchaincyf)
extensions.gives: Art-style animation that stays alive (36 implemented style scenes from cave painting to Monet, Van Gogh, Bauhaus, 8-bit and Ghibli, plus 17 research cards), 9 explainer grammars (Kurzgesagt, Vox, whiteboard, 3Blue1Brown, storytime, kinetic type, keynote UI, finance charts, presenter) with parameterized clips, a reference-breakdown script, a shot-list lint and a delivery gate against slide-deck films. Upstream version 1.2.0; docs mostly in Chinese.
extensions.studio_uses: Studio bundles its direction method in English (camera, look, explainer grammars, six failure modes, shot-list rules) and an adapted reference-breakdown tool in Motion Graphics Workflow. This optional entry installs the original skill with its style scenes, clip renderer and gates.
extensions.not_for: Copying its showcase films, characters or likenesses (they include generated images of real people), replacing Studio's intake, review and delivery, or presenting a research style card as a finished, verified style.

requires.note: Node.js 22.20+ for the pinned skills CLI 1.7.2 install route.
uv runs its Python scripts; FFmpeg renders and analyses; the first render needs `uv run --with playwright playwright install chromium`, a browser download that is asked for separately.
Rendering, concatenation and reference breakdown.

extensions.rights: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 alchaincyf. Keep LICENSE. Museum paintings in its demos are CC0 open-access originals; its showcase characters, likenesses and films are demonstrations, not assets to reuse. Its skill checks for a newer version with `git ls-remote` at most monthly and writes `.last-update-check` in its folder (write `off` there to stop it); it never updates itself.

extensions.name: ISO-GLOW (April Zhu)
extensions.gives: Interactive isometric hairline figures where whatever is switched on glows in one accent colour, as single HTML pages: devices, buildings, city scenes, exploded diagrams, a 3D mode with three.js (including cleaning up a .glb model) and a solid "Lumen" product-illustration style.
extensions.studio_uses: Studio bundles the look adapted for video in Motion Graphics Workflow: an isometric kit, a bass-driven loudspeaker example and audio_envelope.py, which drives glow from a track. This optional entry installs the original skill for clickable pages.
extensions.not_for: Seekable video renders (its pages animate from clicks and wall-clock time; use Studio's kit), real logos or trademarks on objects, or removing its footer credit without the user's choice.

requires.note: Any browser opens the result. Python 3 is optional (the page-assembly step has a manual fallback); curl, shasum and unzip for the pinned install.

extensions.rights: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 April Zhu, built on iso-figure, Copyright (c) 2026 Tolga Cohce (MIT). Keep LICENSE with the skill. Pages end with a small "Made with ISO-GLOW" link that the user may remove; finished figures belong to the user.
